html:
Mecca is a city in a dry valley of the Hejaz in western Arabia, the birthplace of the prophet Muhammad and the holiest city of Islam. Muslims everywhere pray facing its shrine, the Kaaba.

Before Islam it was a shrine town and a trading centre run by the tribe of Quraysh, whose caravans went north to Syria and south to Yemen. Muhammad was born there around 570 and began preaching there around 610. Opposition from the Quraysh drove him and his followers to Medina in the Hijra of 622. He returned in 630, took the city almost without a fight, and cleared the Kaaba of idols.

After that the city's role was religious. The capitals of the caliphs were elsewhere, but every year the Hajj brought pilgrims from across the Muslim world, and with them a great market. The most famous pilgrim was Mansa Musa of Mali, who passed through Cairo with a fortune in gold in 1324.

Local sharifs, descendants of Muhammad, governed the city under Egyptian rulers and, after the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517, under the Ottomans. Ibn Saud took it in 1924, and it became part of Saudi Arabia. In 1979 armed militants held its Great Mosque for two weeks in the Grand Mosque seizure.
